en.summary: Gaming costs are soaring, but you might already have access to a vast library of titles without knowing it. Discover the hidden gaming perks within services you already pay for.
en.body:
The cost of diving into new games and the hardware to play them on continues to climb. With expenses like AI integration and tariffs impacting development and production, it's a challenging time for gamers to keep up. Fortunately, the rise of subscription services offers a more affordable way to access a wide range of titles, but you might already be subscribed to more gaming content than you realize.

## Unlocking Games Through Your Streaming Bills

While services like **Xbox Game Pass**, **PlayStation Plus**, and **Nintendo Switch Online** are well-known gateways to extensive game libraries, many consumers overlook the gaming benefits bundled with their existing entertainment subscriptions. The most prominent example is **Netflix**. Millions worldwide subscribe to the streaming giant for its vast library of films and TV shows, but this subscription also grants access to a growing catalog of mobile games. These titles come without any additional cost, ads, or microtransactions, making them a fantastic value. The **Netflix Games** library features a diverse selection, including acclaimed ports of popular games like **Street Fighter IV Champion Edition**, **Into the Breach**, **Sonic Mania Plus**, and **Dead Cells**. Additionally, **Netflix** is expanding its offerings with games based on its own intellectual property, such as **Money Heist: Ultimate Choice** and **Stranger Things 1984**, alongside original creations, demonstrating a serious commitment to interactive entertainment.

## Beyond Netflix: Other Unexpected Gaming Access Points

Beyond **Netflix**, other subscription services are quietly integrating gaming into their offerings. While not always direct game libraries, some platforms offer access to titles you might already own. **EA Play**, for instance, provides subscribers with access to a curated selection of **Electronic Arts** titles, often including early access to new releases and a vault of beloved games. For those invested in the **Microsoft** ecosystem, **Xbox Game Pass** extends beyond its included catalog, allowing subscribers to stream hundreds of games they already own from the Microsoft Store across various tiers. This feature is a significant perk for existing **Xbox** owners looking to maximize their investment. Furthermore, cloud gaming services, while often requiring separate subscriptions, can be surprisingly cost-effective. Services like **NVIDIA GeForce Now** and **Boosteroid** allow you to stream games you've purchased from PC storefronts, essentially turning your existing game collection into a cloud-accessible library. **Apple Arcade** also stands out, offering over 200 premium mobile games for a low monthly fee, with no ads or in-app purchases, making it an accessible entry point for casual players.

## What's Next for Subscription Gaming

As the landscape of gaming continues to evolve, expect more non-gaming services to explore interactive content and for existing platforms to deepen their game offerings. The trend suggests that accessing a wide variety of games will become increasingly tied to bundles and subscriptions, making it crucial for consumers to understand the full value of their current memberships.

content_raw: Gaming has never been more expensive. We're here to investigate why, and help you play more while spending less. Welcome to GameSpot Cheap Week . As part of GameSpot's Cheap Week , we're running through why games and consoles are so expensive these days ( hint: it's a lot of AI and tariffs ). We're also providing some tips for how to save some money. One way of playing games that has become more popular and commonplace these days is by way of a subscription service. Maybe you don't want to sign up for yet another membership--that's entirely understandable--but it's possible you already have a subscription that includes games that you might not have known about. Below, we run through some of the subscription services you might not immediately associate with gaming, so it doesn't include popular programs like Xbox Game Pass, PlayStation Plus, and Nintendo Switch Online, but those are all solid options for playing more games without buying titles outright.  You may already subscribe to a service with games. Netflix  If you are one of the many millions of Netflix subscribers, you also get access to a growing collection of video games. A nice perk of playing games through your Netflix subscription is that it doesn't cost anything extra and there are no in-game ads or microtransactions. Netflix's library of games includes mobile titles and games you can stream to your PC or TV. Some of the available titles on Netflix include ports of existing games like Street Fighter IV Champion Edition, Into the Breach, Sonic Mania Plus, Dead Cells, and Red Dead Redemption. The Netflix Games library also includes games based on Netflix IP, including Money Heist: Ultimate Choice, Love Is Blind Stories, Narcos: Cartel Wars Unlimited, and Stranger Things 1984. Netflix also creates entirely original games, including the recently released horror game Unhinged . Filmmakers David Fincher (Fight Club, Zodiac) and Zach Cregger (Barbarian, Weapons) collaborated with developer Night School Studios on the project. The New York Times The esteemed publication The New York Times has grown and expanded in a lot of cool ways in recent years, including inroads in lite gaming. The company bought Wordle years ago , and that game continues to be free for everyone. However, if you're a NYT subscriber, you get a lot more than just Wordle for your money. The standalone "games only" NYT subscription also includes Spelling Bee, The Crossword, Spelling Bee, Crossplay, Connections, and more. If you subscribe to "All of The Times," you also get these games, along with NYT's news coverage, cooking content, and The Athletic. GTA+ Maybe you subscribed to GTA+ for the numerous in-game perks for GTA Online, but did you know this membership also includes a library of games at no extra charge?  Some of the titles included with GTA+ include GTA V's story mode, Red Dead Redemption, Bully, and LA Noire, along with older GTA games like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories.
